subject: fix write conflict when first creating dbt_temp schema (#584)
message:
fix write conflict when first creating dbt_temp schema (#584)

I believe this fixes the root cause of https://github.com/duckdb/dbt-duckdb/issues/513 

## Problem
Currently, when using MotherDuck with dbt-duckdb, a real temp schema and real tables will be created to store the staging tables, because temp tables are not yet supported. By default this schema is called `dbt_temp`. When running dbt with 2 or more threads, each incremental model will open a transaction that starts with the statement `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS dbt_temp`. The model that gets executed first will cause a catalog change with the `CREATE SCHEMA` statement while its transaction is still open, while the rest of the models will fail with a write-write conflict on that statement. 

## Solution & Considerations
If the schema `dbt_temp` already exists, then the `CREATE SCHEMA` statement will be a no-op, then all incremental models will succeed. 
So ideally, the create schema statement should be run just once at the beginning of a dbt run. But the current implementation allows each model to configure their own temp schema. This means that we won't fully know the name of the schema that needs to be created until processing the model, also that the`CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS {temp_schema_name}` statement in `macros/materializations/incremental.sql` needs to be preserved. 
So the fix will just address the problem of creating the default temp schema `dbt_temp`, by running `CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS  dbt_temp` when initializing the connection.

Fix secrets map/list type handling in DuckDB SQL generation (#609)

* Fix secrets map/list type handling in DuckDB SQL generation

Add support for proper DuckDB map and array syntax when converting
dict and list types in secret parameters to SQL. Previously, these
complex types were incorrectly wrapped in quotes, causing syntax
errors like "Parser Error: syntax error at or near 'TYPE'".

Changes:
- Add _format_value() method to handle dict, list, and scalar types
- Dict values now generate: map {'key': 'value', 'key2': 'value2'}
- List values now generate: array ['item1', 'item2', 'item3']
- Scalar values maintain existing behavior with proper quoting

This fixes issues with ducklake secrets that use metadata_parameters
as a map type, enabling proper conversion from YAML to DuckDB SQL.

subject: Support ducklake database in primary database and add is_ducklake flag to identify motherduck managed ducklake (#625)
message:
Support ducklake database in primary database and add is_ducklake flag to identify motherduck managed ducklake (#625)

Implements the approach mentioned in https://github.com/duckdb/dbt-duckdb/issues/619 to support motherduck-managed ducklake database, which cannot currently be detected because it does not use the `ducklake:` prefix. This is necessary because otherwise dbt treats the managed ducklake database as a regular database then we get ` Not implemented Error: Cascade Drop not supported in DuckLake`.

Also make it possible to have a primary database that is ducklake (both regular `ducklake:...` and motherduck-managed ducklake db), because it is surprising that it didn't work. But since there's no aliasing, the database name will have to be inferred from the path and may not work for all paths. 

## Testing plan
- [x] Unit tests
- [x] ran some example dbt projects with local and motherduck ducklakes. Here are some profiles I tested. When there are additional attached databases, some of the models are routed to those databases.

```
    ducklake_md:
      type: duckdb
      schema: main
      path: 'md:my_ducklake'
      threads: 1
      is_ducklake: true
      disable_transactions: false
      extensions:
        - httpfs

    ducklake_local:
      type: duckdb
      schema: main
      path: 'ducklake:my_ducklake.ddb'
      threads: 1
      disable_transactions: false
      extensions:
        - httpfs
    
    mixed_md:
      type: duckdb
      path: 'md:my_ducklake3'
      is_ducklake: true
      schema: test
      threads: 1
      attach:
        - path: "md:my_not_ducklake"
        - path: "md:my_other_ducklake"
          is_ducklake: true
    
    mixed_local:
      type: duckdb
      path: 'ducklake:my_ducklake3.ddb'
      schema: test
      threads: 1
      attach:
        - path: "my_not_ducklake.ddb"
        - path: "ducklake:my_other_ducklake.ddb"
 ```

The 3rd one needed this fix https://github.com/duckdb/dbt-duckdb/pull/626

subject: Break out create temp schema into its own transaction (#638)
message:
Break out create temp schema into its own transaction (#638)

addresses https://github.com/duckdb/dbt-duckdb/issues/636

The default incremental Python model (intermediate result) materialization path will [use a new cursor to create a temp table](https://github.com/duckdb/dbt-duckdb/blob/ae5c63f3658f6c296030a07527f61473367e4d0f/dbt/adapters/duckdb/environments/__init__.py#L282-L289). 

This does not work when connected to MotherDuck and with transaction enabled (the setting is `disable_transaction: false`- which is the default), because the incremental model transaction currently wraps all of (`create temp schema`, `delete from target table`, `insert into target table`, `drop temp table`) inside one transaction, and the result of the materialization query, which happens between `create temp schema` and `delete from target table`, will not be visible to the transaction. 

The reason this works for local DuckDB is that local DuckDB uses a real temp table, which does not require a temp schema to be created, so the transaction starts after the materialiaztion query. 

There's no strong reason to include the create temp schema query in the transaction, so we break it out of the main transaction, such that the main transaction starts after the materialization query for the MotherDuck code path.

subject: Fix transaction commit error when no upstream external models exist (#679)
message:
Fix transaction commit error when no upstream external models exist (#679)

Change upstream_nodes check to upstream_schemas in register_upstream_external_models macro.
This ensures we only commit when schemas are actually created, preventing
'Tried to commit transaction on connection "master", but it does not have one open!'
errors when executing models without upstream external models.

Fixes #678

subject: fix: rollback transaction in exception handler (#684)
message:
fix: rollback transaction in exception handler (#684)

* fix: actually rollback transaction in exception handler

The exception handler logged "Rolling back transaction" but never
actually executed the rollback, leaving transactions open after errors.
This could cause locks not being released and resource leaks.
